Synthetic scale fixture (development only, SquashFS **v4**, run the oracle with
`--dev-allow-v4`).  It exists to exercise the parsers on a real tree at scale,
with awkward names and every non-regular kind; v4 is never part of the C1
contract.

Built 2026-10-26 with squashfs-tools 4.7.5 (`mksquashfs version 4.7.5
(2026/03/01)`); image sha256
c5ee82b562f9b6850c8a1a9a142526945fd62c0aefa6c124e2f5f3361e478390, 12288 bytes.

    mkdir -p src && cd src
    python3 - <<'PY'
    import os
    names = ["a b.txt", "plus+name", "eq=name", "arrow -> name", "ümlaut.txt",
             "dash-name.conf", "colon:name", "bracket[1].bin", "quote'name",
             "semi;name", "dollar$name", "amp&name", "percent%20name",
             "hash#name", "at@name", "tilde~name"]
    os.makedirs("a/b/c/d/e/f/g/h"); os.makedirs("links"); os.makedirs("nodes")
    for i in range(300):
        d = os.path.join("dir%02d" % (i % 25), "sub%02d" % (i % 7))
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        p = os.path.join(d, "file%03d_%s" % (i, names[i % len(names)]))
        open(p, "wb").write(bytes([i % 256]) * (i * 7 % 4096 + 1))
    os.symlink("../dir00/sub00/file000_a b.txt", "links/rel-escape")
    os.symlink("/etc/hostname", "links/absolute")
    os.symlink("missing-target", "links/dangling")
    os.symlink("..", "links/dotdot")
    open("a/b/c/d/e/f/g/h/leaf.txt", "w").write("deep\n")
    PY
    mkfifo nodes/pipe
    python3 -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind('nodes/sock'); s.close()"
    mksquashfs . ../img.sqfs -comp gzip -noappend -quiet \
        -p 'nodes/console c 644 0 0 5 1' -p 'nodes/ttyS0 c 600 0 0 4 64' \
        -p 'nodes/loop0 b 660 0 0 7 0'

Result: 520 entries - 301 regular, 210 dir, 4 symlink, 2 char-device,
1 block-device, 1 fifo, 1 socket; all producers agree, 0 mismatches, and the
device numbers in `nonregular.tsv` come from unsquashfs (backhand and 7z cannot
materialise devices).  No third-party bytes: the tree is generated by the recipe
above, which is why this fixture may live in the lane while the OpenWrt images
may not.
